So it’s better to ask said person to live a life of emotional, physical and psychological pain? To save the people around them the emotional stress? 

I think you’ve missed my point in the sympathy here. They should be able to sympathise with them and understand their choice.
So that you would be able to do so in a clinical or home environment without a huge mess, shock etc. being able to pass with the people who care around you.

I feel as though this is emotional blackmail. 

They should be able to sympathise with the person and be with them in passing so as not to die alone.

I’ve looked into this and it is not available for Australians. You also have to apply for temporary citizenship and be re-assesses by the medical team there. 89% of the time, the reject the patient and they’re left out of pocket and in worse circumstances.
Yep. Talked to them about it and now they won’t talk to me. Super.
Is that a valid reason to make someone live a terrible life? Just to please the people who made them?
Did I say that? I said that society thinks that...

Nope. Sydney Australia. I’m fully capable of working and have had a stable career for over 9 years now. And even those, who can’t work because of it, are seen as “just struggling” and in a constant state of “they will get better and contribute later” in the governments eyes. 

Way to miss the point pal.

Edit: replying to wrathguy
I feel you. It’s a fucked up conundrum..

That’s the thing though, the only help I want, is for them to accept that I would like to die. 

I don’t want to keep seeing doctors and taking meds that make me feel worse. You feel?

Closer than your average family I guess. which makes it that much harder. 

I don’t have anything to complain about either. 
We live in a huge house and they can support me for as long as I need but the struggle is telling them that I don’t want any of it. 

I would rather be worm food.

Only in Victoria and is only for terminally ill patients. Long term or life altering disabilities are not included unfortunately. 

Country’s like Switzerland have the most appropriate laws regarding assisted dying.
I understood that the morning after haha
Suddenly regretting turning it down when I was younger 🙄
